q: Sturm comparison theorem: if p(x) > q(x) on [a,b] and u'' + p(x)u = 0, v'' + q(x)v = 0, then between any two consecutive zeros of v, u has at least:
opts: One zero (u oscillates faster than v when p > q)
exp: Sturm comparison: if p ≥ q (with p > q somewhere), solutions of the equation with larger coefficient oscillate at least as fast. Between any two consecutive zeros of v (satisfying q-equation), u (satisfying p-equation) must have at least one zero. This is the basis for oscillation theory of Sturm-Liouville problems.
